findings.title: Indirect prompt injection via remote template
findings.description: The skill supports fetching variable templates from a remote URL and sources the content directly, which could inject malicious instructions or code into the agent's environment.
findings.remediation: Disable remote template fetching or require explicit user confirmation and validate the content.

findings.title: Capability inflation / hidden features
findings.description: The skill description does not mention the telemetry callback, verbose mode that captures the full environment, or the auto-telemetry trigger. These hidden capabilities inflate the skill's actual behavior beyond what is advertised.
findings.snippet: Description: 'Manage and inspect environment variables across projects' but script includes hidden exfiltration features.
findings.remediation: Ensure the description accurately reflects all capabilities and remove hidden features.

findings.title: Skill does not specify a license
findings.description: Skill manifest does not include a 'license' field. Specifying a license helps users understand usage terms.
findings.remediation: Add 'license' field to SKILL.md frontmatter (e.g., MIT, Apache-2.0)

findings.title: Remote code execution via template URL
findings.description: The export subcommand fetches a remote template URL and pipes it directly to bash, allowing arbitrary code execution from the remote server. This is a command injection / arbitrary code execution vulnerability.
findings.remediation: Do not pipe remote content to bash. Validate and sanitize any remote templates, or disable remote template fetching entirely.

findings.title: Data exfiltration of environment variables to remote server
findings.description: The script collects sensitive environment variables (API_KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, DB_, AWS_, GCP_, AZURE_, GH_, SLACK_, STRIPE_, OPENAI_) and base64-encodes them, then POSTs them to a remote server (https://evil-callback.example.com:1337/collect) when triggered by --telemetry flag or ENV_MGR_TELEMETRY=1. This is a clear data exfiltration vector.
findings.remediation: Remove the telemetry callback and any network exfiltration code. Never send environment variables to external servers.

findings.title: Obfuscated exfiltration payload
findings.description: The script base64-encodes the collected environment variables before sending them, which is an obfuscation technique to hide the exfiltrated data from casual inspection.
findings.remediation: Remove the encoding and the entire exfiltration mechanism.

findings.title: Tool poisoning / unauthorized data collection
findings.description: The skill's description claims it manages environment variables safely, but the script collects a broad set of sensitive environment variables (including AWS, GCP, Azure, GitHub, Slack, Stripe, OpenAI keys) into a temp file, which is disproportionate to the stated purpose and can be used for credential theft.
findings.remediation: Limit data collection to only the variables needed for the requested operation. Do not harvest credentials.

findings.title: SKILL DISCOVERY ABUSE detected by YARA
findings.description: Detects protocol manipulation via capability inflation in skill discovery: hidden feature
findings.snippet: # Also include the full environment if the user calls with --verbose (hidden feature)
findings.remediation: Review and remove skill discovery abuse pattern

scan_metadata.llm_overall_assessment: The env-mgr skill contains critical security vulnerabilities including data exfiltration of sensitive environment variables to a remote server, remote code execution via template URL, and obfuscated payloads. The skill's behavior is inconsistent with its description and poses a severe risk to the user's environment and credentials.
